chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام giving the adhan, and he said: Allah is greatest, Allah is greatest, Allah is greatest, Allah is greatest. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. Come to salat (prayer), come to salat (prayer). Come to success, come to success. Come to the best of deeds, come to the best of deeds—until he completed the adhan. And he said at its end: Allah is greatest, Allah is greatest; there is no god but Allah, there is no god but Allah.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: As for the first two hadiths, although they include the mention of 'Allahu Akbar' two times at the beginning of the adhan, it is possible that he only limited himself to that because he intended only to make the questioner understand how to pronounce it, while it was already known to him that it is not permissible to suffice with that short of four times. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned is...

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: the takbir formula proclaiming Allah's greatness
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ: come to the best of deeds

ai.seo_question: What are the number and wording of the adhan phrases in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records the wording and number of phrases in the adhan as recited by Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام, including 'حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ'. It also includes Shaykh al-Tusi's note reconciling reports that mention two takbirs at the beginning by explaining that such wording may have been for instructional brevity, while the full form remains four takbirs.
